items.title: Budget limit increased to 40,000 budgets per account
items.author: Allison
items.excerpt: You can now create up to 40,000 budgets per GitHub Enterprise Cloud account, up from 10,000. If you set budgets for individual users, or manage budgets across many cost centers and organizations, you can keep adding budgets as your enterprise grows. The higher limit applies automatically on github.com and GHE.com, so there’s nothing to turn on. To learn more, see Budgets and alerts. items.title: Bulk start AI Scan for repositories
items.author: Allison
items.excerpt: AI Scan for repositories finds security vulnerabilities on your repository’s default branch. It covers languages CodeQL doesn’t support and finds additional issues in languages CodeQL already analyzes. Findings appear in your code scanning backlog alongside CodeQL alerts. You can now start AI Scans for up to 20 repositories at once. Start scans for selected repositories when you enable the organization-level setting, or from the code scanning organization alerts page. You can also start a scan for an individual repository from its alerts page. Bulk start for AI Scan for repositories is in public preview. AI Scan for repositories is available on github.com and GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency. A GitHub Copilot license isn’t required. Learn more about AI Scan and join the discussion in GitHub Community. The post Bulk start AI Scan for repositories appeared first on The GitHub Blog.
items.why_it_matters: GitHub's AI Scan can now be started on up to 20 repositories at once. It makes it easier to run vulnerability scans across client repos alongside CodeQL.

items.title: GitHub Copilot models deprecated on November 16, 2026

Note that Claude Opus 4.8 is still available to individual GitHub Copilot subscribers on annual plans. These deprecations were announced on October 15, 2026. the terminal now warns and names it Fixed a failed MCP header

items.title: Building Visual Intelligence — Andreas Blattmann & Dustin Podell, Black Forest Labs
items.author: swyx .ai
items.excerpt: This episode is sponsored by Deepgram. Try Deepgram for voice agents that truly understand your context! #contextiseverything Not many people know that Stable Diffusion is why I went fulltime into AI (I aptly titled Multiverse, not Metaverse to call out Zuck’s mistaken investment). It turns out that Dustin Podell also had the same aha moment - quitting his day job when the model came out. But we took very different paths… I stuck to what I knew in human content creation, and Dustin immersed deep into AI content creation with Andreas Blattmann, co-inventor of Latent Diffusion and the rest of the world-leading imagegen crew at Stability AI. Stability fell apart, but Anj Midha helped the core group spin out to BFL, which immediately built an incredible new imagegen model in the Flux series. But why are they now going into video and world models? Andreas gives an example you can try with one hand. If somebody tosses you a ball, your hand starts moving before the ball reaches you. You can do that without being able to write down the trajectory. When he talks about building visual intelligence, that’s the kind of knowledge he means. A still can show you where the ball is. A video shows you how it got there. The sound of impact can tell you when it hit something, even if the camera missed the contact. That’s BFL’s argument for training FLUX 3 on the three signals together. BFL’s FLUX 3 releaseThe horse in motion is one of the FLUX 3 examples we show in the intro. The audio examples are worth playing with the sound on. FLUX 3 VideoWhat a moving camera teaches you Suppose the camera starts in front of a person and pans around them. At some point the model owes you the back of their head. Andreas thinks ordinary two-dimensional video contains a great deal of evidence about what objects look like from other angles. That doesn’t settle whether a model “understands physics,” a point we go back and forth on. It does give you a much better test than asking whether one frame looks

items.title: datasette 1.0a43
items.excerpt: Release: datasette 1.0a43 I've been leaning hard into Claude Fable 5.2 to help knock things off the 1.0 milestone, which is now 53% complete. The biggest 1.0 item in this release is streaming support for output renderers - the built-in TSV and CSV export mechanisms now use this as well, and plugins can register themselves as capable of streaming every row in a table in one go via the new Response.stream() method. There are a couple of security fixes, one of which I deemed deserving of a GitHub advisory: private stored queries could be exposed, granting access to the title and SQL of the query (but not allowing that query to be executed). There are dozens of smaller improvements. The row page JSON representation finally has a design suitable for 1.0. A new <datasette-copy-button> Web Component provides copy-schema in various places. JSON in columns on the row page can be pretty-printed. There's a new DatasetteModal.confirm() JavaScript utility method. Plus dozens of bug fixes, including contributions by Zihan Dai, Peter Olkhovets, Ilya Khalafi, and Ankita Advitot. The feature I'm most excited about is a pretty tiny one: I've added CSS multi-page view transitions to Datasette! Here's the commit - key CSS is as follows: /* Enable cross-document view transitions, for anyone without prefers-reduced-motion */ @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) { @view-transition { navigation: auto; } } /* .facet-results should morph from old position to new */ html:active-view-transition .content > .facet-results { view-transition-name: facet-results; } /* So should a .table-wrapper, provided it contains .rows-and-columns */ html:active-view-transition .table-wrapper:has(> table.rows-and-columns) { view-transition-name: rows-table; } With that in place, navigations within Datasette - still staunchly a multi-page application - feel more like an SPA. This works on Safari and Chrome at the moment and I believe supports for Firefox is due to land in Firefox 162 on December 8th 202
items.why_it_matters: Datasette 1.0a43 adds streaming renderers and fixes a security bug that exposed private stored queries. It also shows Claude-assisted maintenance, but Datasette isn't in our stack.

items.title: datasette-apps 0.4a0
items.excerpt: Release: datasette-apps 0.4a0 Datasette Apps are sandboxed HTML and JavaScript applications that live inside Datasette - think Claude Artifacts, but these ones can run SQL queries against your data. 0.4a0 adds support for linking: you can link to an app with #fragments in the URL and the app can see and use those, plus supported URL schemes are reported back to Datasette Agent so it can help write apps that link to each other. This means you can have e.g. an app that shows details about a specific record, and a completely separate app that searches those records and links to their representations in the first app. Tags: datasette-agent, datasette-apps, datasette, urls

items.title: datasette-maplibre 0.1a0
items.excerpt: Release: datasette-maplibre 0.1a0 The first new Datasette geospatial plugin in quite a while! This one combines the excellent MapLibre GL library with OpenFreeMap, the free vector map server operated by Zsolt Ero (you should sponsor Zsolt on GitHub.) I built most of this with a single prompt to Claude Fable 5.2: Look at datasette-cluster-map and datasette-leaflet-geojson plugins, then look at ~/dev/tools/openfreemap-demo.html - then build a brand new Datasette plugin that uses maplibreGL and openfreemap and combines the features of those other two plugins - but be creative and think outside the box for other useful features the plugin might have "Be creative and think outside the box" resulted in a few neat ideas - my favorite is that it displays SVG previews of GeoJSON shapes, then loads a WebGL preview only when they scroll into view. I also had Claude build a comprehensive demo which works in the latest Datasette Lite, so you can visit this link to load the plugin and a demo database in your browser via Pyodide and WebAssembly. I like this demo page showing both GeoJSON shapes and lat/lon points on the same map: Tags: visualization, generative-ai, datasette-lite, claude-mythos-fable, ai, llms, geospatial, openstreetmap, datasette

items.title: Why FLUX 3 Trains on Images, Video and Sound — Andreas Blattmann & Dustin Podell, Black Forest Labs
items.author: Latent Space
items.excerpt: A camera moves around a person. Halfway around, the model has to draw the back of a head it has never seen. How much can it learn about that missing view just by watching video? That’s the question we put to Andreas Blattmann and Dustin Podell of Black Forest Labs. Their answer runs through FLUX 3. BFL trained one backbone on images, video and audio. The guests explain what each adds, how they decide which parts of denoising deserve the most compute, and why a detail that looks great in a still can flicker from frame to frame. We also get into the case for autoregression and where they think diffusion still has an edge. There’s personal history here. Stable Diffusion is why Dustin left his software job and why swyx started Latent Space. They revisit the first FLUX training run in a French chalet, the photo experiment behind FLUX Kontext, and some of the things people actually use these models for, from restoring old family photos to generating a clip with synchronized sound. This episode is sponsored by Deepgram. Build a voice agent at https://deepgram.com/contextiseverything Chapters 0:00 Host introduction 3:39 Cold open 4:23 Black Forest roots 9:23 Dustin’s path 17:04 Visual intelligence 27:38 Inside SDXL 33:59 Learning motion 39:57 Flow matching 46:57 Starting BFL 50:36 Deepgram sponsor break 51:43 Early use cases for FLUX 54:58 Editing with Kontext 1:03:15 Training data 1:07:32 Testing an edit 1:13:12 Autoregression 1:20:50 World action models 1:30:08 Robotics in 2027 1:32:16 Who uses FLUX? Show notes • BFL’s account of why it trained FLUX 3 across images, video and audio — https://bfl.ai/blog/flux-3 • Watch FLUX 3 generate video with synchronized sound — https://bfl.ai/blog/flux-3-video • Try the night-to-day image edit mentioned in the episode — https://bfl.ai/models/flux-kontext • Andreas Blattmann co-created Stable Diffusion and co-invented latent diffusion — https://raais.co/speakers-2025-andreas-blattmann-black-forest-labs • Dustin Podell led FLUX Kontext

items.title: Fable 5.2 is CRACKED but THIS goes BEYOND THE MODEL
items.author: IndyDevDan
items.excerpt: Fable 5.2 just dropped and most engineers DON'T need it. Everyone has access to the same frontier intelligence. The model is NOT your edge. The system you build around the model is. One super agent that does everything is a myth. Sub-agents hit a ceiling. Agent swarms burn more money than they make. The real multi-agent sweet spot? Small agent teams. 🚀 Phase 3 PRE-LAUNCH IS LIVE (What if your agents never stopped?) https://agenticengineer.com/infinite-agentic-engineering?y=hYIymEMB9x4 🔥 In Tiny Software Factories (TSF) Lesson 3, IndyDevDan breaks down small agent teams: a handful of specialized agents, each owning one kind of work, led by a single orchestrator. Picture two agents on the same model. One is generic, with default tools and a context window stuffed with every problem. The other has focused tools, focused context, and a focused system prompt loaded with your team's rules and expertise. The focused agent wins every time, the same way a focused engineer wins. ⚡ Quick Fable 5.2 mention: it's an incredible leap, but you only need it if you're writing massive 500 line specs, hill climbing in a recursive self-improving loop, or running multi-agent orchestration. That third bucket is where software factories get interesting. The system card shows a five agent team beating both a single agent and a pile of async agents. And the real surprise on Artificial Analysis isn't max mode. It's Fable 5.2 medium and low, still out-scoring 70% of the top models at a fraction of the cost. Use it as an orchestrator with workhorse models below it. But remember, the model is just one fourth of the core four: context, model, prompt, tools. 🏭 Every software factory starts as an empty factory. Why? So you can customize it. This is liquid software, designed to be reshaped to YOUR problem. 🛠️ Key takeaways: Small Agent Teams: Several specialized, durable agents inside one factory, each with its own core four, list, and lane. Hit tilde to open the team switcher and jump between agent
